attempts.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) to serve DHCP on lan-a (eth2, 10.50.10.0/24) to node3, and node2 (OPNsense) to serve DHCP on lan-b (opt2/vtnet2, 10.60.10.0/24) to node4, each router handing out its own interface address as the default gateway. Topology was first mapped empirically (broadcast/ARP probing) since no prior mapping was given: node1 eth2 <-> node3 eth1, node2 vtnet2 <-> node4 eth1. On node2, discovered and permanently disabled a conflicting factory-default dnsmasq DHCP/DNS placeholder (bound to wildcard UDP/67) that blocked Kea from binding on the new interface; fixed it via the proper OPNsense config.xml + template-reload path so it survives reboot. All four nodes were then restarted one at a time (native reboot) with captured pre/post boot-identity proof and post-restart verification that addressing, routing, and DHCP services fully recovered.
